While parsing the PoC's `<m xml:id="a"/>`, the special xml:id path registers the attribute node `ret` in `doc->ids` under the attacker-chosen value `a`. The stored entry keeps `id->attr = ret` for later `xmlGetID` lookups.
After the reader advances from `<m>` to the following `<xi:include>` sibling, streaming cleanup selects the previous `<m>` node as `tmp` and recursively frees that subtree.
Cleanup reaches the xml:id attribute as `cur`, but the no-DTD PoC document makes this guard false. `xmlTextReaderRemoveID` is therefore skipped even though step 1 already placed `cur` in `doc->ids`.

The xml:id attribute lifetime ends as property cleanup frees the attribute object, but because step 3 skipped ID removal the document ID table still retains `id->attr = cur`. The enclosing `<m>` subtree is being retired by the same recursive cleanup, so the stale attribute's `parent` will no longer point to a live element either.

Once the current streamed node is the PoC's `xi:include` element in the XInclude namespace, the reader enters XInclude processing on that node after the earlier xml:id-bearing subtree has already been retired.
XInclude evaluates the fragment string derived from `href="#a"`. The attacker-controlled identifier `a` is now the XPointer expression that will be resolved against the current document.
For a bare-name XPointer, the fragment name is pushed as a string and dispatched to XPath id() resolution, turning the attacker-controlled name `a` into an ID-table lookup request.
The ID lookup returns the stored attribute pointer from `doc->ids`. Because step 4 left the table entry stale, this returned `id->attr` is the freed xml:id attribute rather than a live node.

xmlXPathGetElementsByIds treats the stale pointer as an attribute node and reloads `elem` from `attr->parent`. That converts the freed attribute into a dangling pointer to the freed `<m>` element, which is then passed onward to nodeset insertion.
Nodeset insertion dereferences the dangling element pointer as `val` by reading `val->type`. This is the AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free read reported in the staged crash trace.
Parsing the attacker-controlled xml:id attribute registers that live xmlAttrPtr in the document ID table for later id() lookups.
Streaming attribute cleanup only removes IDs when a DTD subset exists, even though xml:id attributes were registered in doc->ids without any DTD.
The freed element pointer recovered from the stale ID lookup is dereferenced when xmlXPathNodeSetAdd reads its type.
